title: Syntomic algebras lift along arbitrary ring surjections
statement: Let $\pi:R\twoheadrightarrow R_0$ be a surjective homomorphism of commutative rings with identity, and put $I=\ker\pi$. For any homomorphism $T\to B$ of commutative rings, call it syntomic if $B$ is flat as a $T$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], is a finitely presented $T$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], and for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset T$ the fibre algebra $B\otimes_T\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is a local complete intersection over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product, def-weil-residue-field, def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]. Here $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is the fraction field of $T/\mathfrak p$. Let $B_0$ be a commutative $R_0$-algebra with $R_0\to B_0$ syntomic. There exist a commutative $R$-algebra $B$, with $R\to B$ syntomic, and an isomorphism of $R_0$-algebras $\beta:B/IB\xrightarrow{\sim}B_0$, where the $R_0$-structure on $B/IB$ is induced by $R/I\cong R_0$. No nilpotence, Noetherianity, locality, or characteristic hypothesis on $R$ or $R_0$ is imposed; the zero algebra is allowed.

source.place: Tag 07M8, proposition-lift-smooth, assertion (1). Syntomic is expanded using algebra.tex Tag 00SL, definition-lci; the zero-ring convention is algebra.tex Tag 00S9, definition-lci-field.

proof.text: If $B_0=0$, take $B=0$: it is flat, has presentation $R/(1)$, and every fibre is zero, hence lci by the stated convention. Otherwise choose a finite polynomial presentation $B_0=R_0[u_1,\ldots,u_n]/J_0$ using finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. By [lem-sfb-syntomic-presentation-conormal-fibre-rank], $P_0=J_0/J_0^2$ is finite projective. Put $C_0=\operatorname{Sym}_{B_0}(P_0)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-projective-presentation-conormal] this specific symmetric algebra has a surjective finite polynomial presentation with free conormal. It is smooth over $B_0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-finite-projective-smooth]; [lem-sfb-syntomic-smooth-composition] therefore makes $R_0\to C_0$ syntomic. In particular it is finitely presented. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-conormal-free-presentation-basis] to obtain $C_0=R_0[y_1,\ldots,y_m]/(\bar f_1,\ldots,\bar f_c)$ with these equations a basis of the conormal.

For a prime $\mathfrak p\subset R_0$ and any point of the nonempty fibre of $C_0$, [lem-sfb-syntomic-presentation-conormal-fibre-rank] applied to the basis presentation of step 1 gives local topological fibre dimension $m-c$, since that conormal has rank $c$ after base change. Hence this fibre $F$ has Krull dimension $m-c$: by the definition of dimension at a point each point $\mathfrak q$ has an open neighbourhood $U_{\mathfrak q}$ of dimension exactly $m-c$, so $\dim F\ge m-c$; conversely, for a chain $Z_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq Z_k$ of irreducible closed subsets of $\operatorname{Spec}F$ pick $\mathfrak q\in Z_0$; the traces $Z_i\cap U_{\mathfrak q}$ are nonempty, irreducible and closed in $U_{\mathfrak q}$, with closures $Z_i$, hence form a strict chain, so $k\le m-c$. Lift the finitely many coefficients of each $\bar f_j$ along $R\twoheadrightarrow R_0$ to obtain $f_j\in R[y_1,\ldots,y_m]$. Put $\widetilde C=R[y_1,\ldots,y_m]/(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$. Coefficient reduction gives $\widetilde C/I\widetilde C\cong C_0$, by the universal property of the polynomial quotient. Apply [lem-sfb-equation-count-closed-fibre-localization] and replace $\widetilde C$ by $C=\widetilde C_g$, where $g$ reduces to $1$. Its reduction remains $C_0$ (a fraction $s/g^e$ reduces to $\bar s$), and $C$ is a relative global complete intersection.

The map $R\to C$ is syntomic. Write $C\cong R[y_1,\ldots,y_m,z]/(f_1,\ldots,f_c,hz-1)$ for the relative global complete intersection presentation of step 2. It is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection-flat], and finitely presented by this presentation [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. For a prime $\mathfrak q\subset R$, [lem-weil-pbc-presentation-base-change] presents the fibre $C\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ as $\kappa(\mathfrak q)[y_1,\ldots,y_m,z]$ modulo the coefficientwise images of $f_1,\ldots,f_c,hz-1$, with $m+1$ variables and $c+1$ equations. If the fibre is nonzero, its Krull dimension is $(m+1)-(c+1)$ by [def-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection], so it is a global complete intersection over $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$; if it is zero, it is one by the zero-ring convention. In both cases the one-element family $g=1$ shows that it is a local complete intersection over $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field].

Choose a finite projective complement $Q_0$ with $P_0\oplus Q_0\cong B_0^{\oplus r}$. This is the direct-summand meaning of finite projectivity. Tensor this split decomposition with $C_0$ to see that $Q_0\otimes_{B_0}C_0$ is finite projective over $C_0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-lift-projective-module-etale] to the ring $C$, the ideal $IC$ and this module. It supplies an etale map $C\to C^\prime$ inducing $C/IC\cong C^\prime/IC^\prime$, and a finite projective $C^\prime$-module $Q$ reducing to $Q_0\otimes_{B_0}C_0$. Set $D=\operatorname{Sym}_{C^\prime}(Q)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-finite-projective-smooth] the map $C^\prime\to D$ is smooth. Applying [lem-sfb-syntomic-smooth-composition] twice to $R\to C\to C^\prime\to D$ shows that $R\to D$ is syntomic.

By [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-base-change] the reduction of $D$ is $\operatorname{Sym}_{C_0}(Q_0\otimes_{B_0}C_0)\cong C_0\otimes_{B_0}\operatorname{Sym}_{B_0}(Q_0)$. Since $C_0=\operatorname{Sym}_{B_0}(P_0)$, [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-universal-property] identifies this with $\operatorname{Sym}_{B_0}(P_0\oplus Q_0)\cong B_0[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$: maps from either algebra into any commutative $B_0$-algebra are precisely pairs of linear maps from $P_0$ and $Q_0$, or, using the chosen decomposition, arbitrary images of the $r$ basis vectors. The inverse maps agree on scalars and these generating modules, so uniqueness in the cited universal property makes them inverse. In the reduction comparison the usual tensor-quotient maps are $d\otimes\bar c\mapsto\overline{cd}$ and $\bar d\mapsto d\otimes1$. All the resulting isomorphisms preserve the $R_0$-algebra structures.

Lift the variables $x_i$ to elements $t_i\in D$ by surjectivity of $D\to D/ID$, and set $A=D/(t_1,\ldots,t_r)$. The reduction is $A/IA\cong B_0[x_1,\ldots,x_r]/(x_1,\ldots,x_r)\cong B_0$, by evaluation at zero. Apply [lem-sfb-syntomic-polynomial-fibre-cut] to the syntomic algebra $D$ from step 4 and the reduction isomorphism of step 5. Its hypotheses on $A_0=B_0$ are exactly the original syntomic hypothesis (identify $R/I$ with $R_0$ through $\pi$). We obtain $a\in A$ reducing to $1$, with $B=A_a$ syntomic over $R$.

The map $B\to B_0$ sends $u/a^e$ to the image of $u$ under $A\to A/IA\cong B_0$. Since $a$ reduces to $1$, it induces an isomorphism $\beta:B/IB\cong B_0$, with inverse the map from $A/IA$ induced by $u\mapsto u/1$. These maps are inverse on every fraction and on every residue class. They preserve scalars through $R/I\cong R_0$, so $\beta$ is an $R_0$-algebra isomorphism as required.
